blocks.text: GOVERNOR OF JUDAH UNDER BABYLON · TWO KINGDOMS
Gedaliah. Governor at Mizpah over the poor of the land; murdered in the seventh month.
GOVERNEDi
Not given c. 586 BC (dates vary)
SEAT
Mizpah
HOUSE
Son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan 3rd of 5 in Babylon
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“He swore to the captains: "Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king…”
PROPHETS
Jeremiah
BABYLON: 5 RULERS MERODACH-BALADAN → BELSHAZZAR
AUTHORITY
Under whose authority
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
He swore to the captains: "Fear not to be the servants of the Chaldees: dwell in the land, and serve the king of Babylon; and it shall be well with you." 2 Kings 25:24
"As for me, behold, I will dwell at Mizpah to serve the Chaldeans, which will come unto us: but ye, gather ye wine, and summer fruits, and oil." Jeremiah 40:10
Warned that Ishmael meant to kill him, "Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not", and forbade Johanan to strike first: "thou speakest falsely of Ishmael". Jeremiah 40:14–16
Ishmael "smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land". Jeremiah 41:2
THE KINGDOM
Mizpah and the places of the reign
Babylon. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
Two days after his death eighty men from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria came mourning "with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the LORD". Jeremiah 41:4–5

Scholars' viewJoseph Benson (about 1815) and James Crichton (1915) connect the "fast of the seventh month" in Zechariah with Gedaliah's murder; Zechariah does not name him. Zechariah 7:5 Zechariah 8:19 [43][18]

What each book tells

JEREMIAH
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
Appointed after the burning of Jerusalem in the fifth month of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year; killed in a seventh month.
AFTER JERUSALEM'S FALL IN 586 BC (MCFALL, 1991)
If he was killed in the seventh month of the same year, about two months after the burning (see the question below).
AFTER JERUSALEM'S FALL IN 587 BC (ALBRIGHT, 1945)
Albright dates the city's fall a year earlier.
TO ABOUT 582 BC, IF HIS DEATH CAME WITH THE DEPORTATION OF NEBUCHADNEZZAR'S TWENTY-THIRD YEAR (GRAETZ)
H. Graetz's view, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary: some five years of rule, linking his death to Jeremiah 52:30.
About two months: he was killed in the seventh month of the year Jerusalem fell
C. F. Keil (1880); A. W. Streane (1881); Joseph Benson (about 1815)
They read Jeremiah 41:1's "seventh month" as two months after the burning in the fifth month. Jeremiah 41:1 2 Kings 25:8 [32][42][43]
About five years, ending with the deportation of Nebuchadnezzar's twenty-third year
H. Graetz, as reported by the Pulpit Commentary
Graetz thought the events of Jeremiah 40–41 needed more than two months, and tied Gedaliah's death to the 745 people taken "in the three and twentieth year of Nebuchadrezzar". Jeremiah 52:30 [41]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage

2 Kings 25 Jeremiah 39 Jeremiah 40 Jeremiah 41 Jeremiah 42 Jeremiah 43
PASSAGES · 5
2 Kings 25:22–26 Jeremiah 39:11–14 Jeremiah 40:1–41:18 Jeremiah 42:1 Jeremiah 43:5–7
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give the year of Gedaliah's death, only "the seventh month".
Scripture does not say what became of Ishmael after he fled to the Ammonites.
Scripture names no successor to Gedaliah as governor.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the text"Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan"; his father Ahikam had kept Jeremiah from being put to death. 2 Kings 25:22 Jeremiah 39:14 Jeremiah 26:24
From the textKings calls him first "ruler" and then "governor"; Jeremiah calls him the man "whom the king of Babylon hath made governor over the cities of Judah". 2 Kings 25:22–23 Jeremiah 40:5

links.text: Belshazzar, King of Babylon, as Daniel calls him
Cyrus, King of Persia, Not given in Scripture. Chronicles and Ezra date his proclamation to "the first year of Cyrus king of Persia"; Daniel mentions his first
Darius the Mede, King over the realm of the Chaldeans (Daniel), Not given. Daniel says he took the kingdom "being about threescore and two years old" and dates
Zerubbabel, Governor of Judah, Not given. Haggai calls him "governor of Judah" in the second year of Darius; he is first among the leaders of the return under C
Josiah, King of Judah, Thirty-one years, from the age of eight (2 Kgs 22:1; 2 Chr 34:1)., c. 641–609 BC, did right in the eyes of the LORD
Jehoahaz, King of Judah, Three months, at the age of twenty-three (2 Kgs 23:31; 2 Chr 36:2)., c. 609 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
